To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the most contaminated fraction of RDS is the fine fraction (silt + clay) and that the fine fraction is also the most abundant mass fraction.
road deposited sediment is contaminated with lead and that the lead is concentrated in the fine-grained sediment fractions.

1) road deposited sediment is a significant environmental medium for assessing contamination in urban areas; 2) Pb is highly concentrated in all road deposited sediment samples from Palolo, Oahu, HI; and 3) the silt/clay size fraction is the most important mass component for storing Pb in road-deposited sediments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the most important grain size fraction in RDS for Pb contamination.
the environmental impacts of road-deposits and their management.
the environmental fate of Pb in RDS and the importance of Pb in the smallest grain sizes of RDS.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the most important mass fraction of Pb in road-deposited sediments is stored in the silt and clay size fractions.
the fine-grained fractions of RDS are the primary environmental sink of Pb in urban environments, and the most effective street sweeping programs should focus on these grain-size fractions.
the fine-grained fraction of road sediment is an extremely important component of the total Pb burden in road sediments, and that street sweepers are not removing the fine-grained sediment fraction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the most effective street sweepers should be those that remove the finest fractions of RDS.
the majority of the Pb in the RDS is in the silt and clay fraction, and that street sweepers are not removing this size range.
the majority of the Pb in road-deposited sediments is stored in the finest fractions of the sediment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Pb is not evenly distributed among grain sizes in road-deposited sediments.
street sweeper sediment removal efficiency for fine-grained particles is not as effective as it is for coarser-grained particles.
Pb contamination is ubiquitous in RDS and that the fine grain size fractions are the main contributors to the Pb load in RDS.
